title: TBM Conference 2026: Cracks In The Silos
summary: Learn why AI spend management requires faster financial insights and coordination across TBM, FinOps, Tokenomics, SPM, and CSDM
body_markdown:
AI is creating cracks in the silos that have long separated technology cost, consumption, investment and value management. That was our biggest takeaway from last week’s TBM Conference in Miami. Two ideas in particular changed how we think about what comes next:


### **Change the cadence of financial management**


Last year, the TBM Conference opened itself for the first time to vendor sponsors not named “Apptio”. This year marked another first, as non-Apptio sponsors were on the floor in the expo hall as exhibitors. This included vendors from[Forrester’s ITFM Wave](https://www.forrester.com/report/the-forrester-wave-tm-it-financial-management-software-q2-2026/RES196448) like Serviceware, MagicOrange and Nicus, as well as newcomers like Yarken and Dotwork.


The newcomers offered an interesting approach: natively integrated ITFM, FinOps and Tokenomics capabilities in one platform. We haven’t demoed either offering, but both highlight a persona that legacy ITFM tools often overlook: project managers executing AI-driven use cases. Because AI spend fluctuates constantly and companies are still maturing AI spend control and optimization, monthly GL-driven cost tracking isn’t good enough for project managers; they need to know how yesterday’s token spend impacts where they stand today in order to respond to spikes and keep the initiative on time and on budget. Yarken and Dotwork enable this capability by tabulating estimates for expenses that would otherwise be updated monthly. The tradeoff is that this financial view will not tie to the financial source of truth (i.e., the general ledger) so no one really owns the estimate. But is that so critical as long as it’s reconciled at the end of the month?


### **Treat Standards as Complements, Not Competitors**


Keynotes, presentations and fireside chats repeatedly focused on the need for standards to converge. The reason? Technology investment decisions are getting more attention from CEOs than ever, however no standard provides all the context leaders need. For example:


- Swapna Samuel from BMO gave the best keynote we’ve seen all year on how TBM, FinOps and Tokenomics deliver critical inputs to a broader AI value management chain. It was the clearest representation we’ve seen of how the three standards can be woven together in a single operating model encompassing what’s being consumed, how it’s being consumed, who’s consuming it and what the ultimate value it’s creating is. JR Storment of the Linux Foundation also joined TBM Council Chair Laura Walsh to talk about the importance of TBM, FinOps and Tokenomics working together in the most visible display of collaboration between the TBM Council and the Linux Foundation to date.
- Forrester and Apptio presented on how TBM can tell you all about what tech costs and who’s consuming it. But only when you fold in Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM) can you take that information and make fully informed decisions about portfolio priorities, capacity and timing.
- The TBM Council and ServiceNow announced an initiative to connect the TBM taxonomy to ServiceNow’s common services data model (CSDM) to make the TBM taxonomy native within Service Now. This means ServiceNow will pre-code IT operational data to the TBM taxonomy, providing out-of-the-box mapping between operational and financial data. This is valuable because it enables organizations to attach a standardized view of costs to operational workflows and automatically map operational data to TBM allocation drivers.


The common thread is that managing AI investment decisions requires inputs from TBM, FinOps, Tokenomics, SPM, *and* CSDM. They’ll never form a single model because the personas and use cases of each differ. However, mature AI spend management requires them to work in tandem. This way, leaders have a 360-degree view of a decision rather than multiple views


### **What It Means for You**


The 2026 TBM Conference was a call to action about how you define your AI value management maturity. Ask yourself:


- *Do your IT Finance, FinOps and AI spend management teams communicate and share information? Are they partners in developing the business case and monitoring the success of your most critical AI investments?* Tight collaboration between these disciplines is critical to creating one unified source of truth. If your answer to either question is “no” then these teams need to develop a shared operating model.
- *Do your project managers have day to day visibility into token spend?* They need this in order to course correct in time to avoid cost overruns and delays. So, if they don’t have it, do more to understand the billing capabilities of your AI vendor. Alternatively, use an AI gateway to plug the visibility gap. And if you’re in the market for tooling, at least demo one all-in-one tool.
- *Are you confident the cost and benefit sides of your ROI equation are aligned?* If not, make sure your IT Finance, FinOps and AI spend management teams are meeting with the businesses leaders who own the expected benefits to drive accountability for the outcome. Otherwise, you risk overvaluing the ROI of a use case by bringing in an incomplete picture of the costs.
